name: save-as-dirty-tab
covers: Save As onto a file another tab has open with unsaved edits, spelled differently (case, separators): MarkTheCrab asks Replace/Cancel after the OS replace prompt. Cancel writes nothing; Replace writes, closes the old tab, and no 'modified outside' prompt follows (44c443a). Also: opening the same file under another spelling switches to its tab.

target_path.windows: Windows: $SMOKE\STYLE.MD with backslashes and different case (upper-case the directory name too, e.g. ...\SMOKE-SUITE\STYLE.MD)
target_path.linux: Linux: $SMOKE/sub/../style.md (Linux paths are case-sensitive, so use a '..' segment instead); setup must also mkdir $SMOKE/sub

reopen_path.windows: Windows: like $target_path plus a '.' segment (…\SMOKE-SUITE\.\STYLE.MD). The Open dialog autocompletes a path it has seen back to its on-disk spelling, which would defeat the test; the extra segment keeps it misspelled.

phases.note: Make tab A (style.md) dirty: the editor has focus after launch. Windows: keys without window_id (a key posted to the HWND doesn't reach WebView2).

Windows: invoking the menu bar's File through UIA doesn't open it, so use real keys: F10 (File focused), Down (menu open on New Window), Down x5 to Save As (New Window, New Tab, Open..., Open Recent, Save, Save As...), Return.
Native Save dialog, learned in its own window. Windows has three elements named 'File name:' (label, combobox, edit), so the field needs role 'textfield'.
OS replace prompt (Windows 'Confirm Save As' → Yes; GTK → Replace). Then MarkTheCrab's own prompt, a separate window titled 'Unsaved changes'.

Cancel wrote nothing and both tabs survive. A selected tab's name includes its close button ('style.md Close style.md'), an unselected one doesn't, so tab checks match on the tab role and a name prefix.
Replace wrote the new tab's text, closed tab A, and no 'modified outside' prompt followed within 5 s.

Reopen under another spelling from a fresh tab. Windows: the Open dialog's 'Open' is a split button whose UIA invoke doesn't open the file; press Return in the name field instead (real key, no window_id).

checks.manual: Exactly two tabs (find_elements role 'tabitem' on Windows): one whose name starts with 'style.md' and is 'selected', and 'Untitled' unselected. No third tab.

notes: Windows run 2026-11-09 confirmed every native-dialog name above. Linux dialog titles and names ('Save', 'Name', 'Replace', 'Open', the File menu role) still come from docs: confirm them on the first Linux run. The MarkTheCrab prompt's buttons come from ask() (okLabel 'Replace', cancelLabel 'Cancel'), so those names are ours and stable.
